Drives Microduck, Open Duck Mini, LeRobot, XLeRobot, AlohaMini, ToddlerBot, or any ROS 2 base from a laptop, offboard.
repositories.summary: Command line for hobby robots that can put a decision model (Jev, Laya or Kev) in front of each robot’s LLM brain as an optional discrete stepper.
repositories.boundary: The decision stepper is tested offline against a stub SDK (README).

repositories.description: Camera-only autonomous drone in MuJoCo with a small judgment model (TypeSafe Jev) in the loop at 2.5Hz
repositories.summary: Camera-only quadrotor in MuJoCo in which Jev, at about 2.5 Hz, decides what the situation means while perception and time-critical control stay in code.
repositories.boundary: Jev is not the perception layer; the author notes that the decision step is a small share of the loop time.

repositories.description: Unofficial study: Jev-style parallel typed decisions on stock 1.5B-8B models on an Apple Silicon laptop. Benchmarks, research notes, and a Hugging Face Space demo.
repositories.summary: Unofficial study of Jev-style parallel typed decisions on stock 1.5B–8B models on an Apple Silicon laptop: one prefill, a broadcast KV cache and every field in one forward pass.
repositories.boundary: Untrained stock models; the smallest model scored near the majority-class baseline in the author’s test.

repositories.description: A decision model that returns calibrated answers to yes/no, choice, score and multi-label questions.
repositories.summary: WaterSheep: a ModernBERT-base decision model for yes/no, choice, score and multi-label questions with a probability per option and a Jev-compatible local server.
repositories.boundary: Accuracy falls on datasets held out from training (README).

repositories.description: Get FAR MORE done with FAR FEWER tokens 🔥
repositories.summary: Coding-agent harness and TUI that can let Jev choose the reasoning effort for each step.
repositories.boundary: Jev is one optional routing component; benchmark figures cover the whole harness.

repositories.description: StarCraft II controller combining Jev action selection with GPT-6 planning.
repositories.summary: Macro and micro controllers, winning replays and selected decision logs.
repositories.boundary: Not independently reproduced.

repositories.description: Independent calibration test of TypeSafe's Jev on a task it cannot have seen: 900 rule-generated support tickets (choice / score / boolean) plus 3 public benchmarks via Vercel AI Gateway. Raw responses, ECE with noise floor, temperature refit, per-type sign of miscalibration. Reproducible for ~$0.06.
repositories.summary: Calibration on 3,721 public-benchmark items and 900 synthetic items whose rule is not recoverable from the text; all raw responses published.
repositories.boundary: Called through a gateway alias without a model version; temperature refits are post-hoc diagnostics.

repositories.description: Plain-English browser e2e tests cheap enough to run on every PR. Built on Jev and Playwright, open source, bring your own key.
repositories.summary: Plain-English browser end-to-end tests on Playwright, where a decision model finds the element each sentence refers to and judges whether a claim holds on the page.
repositories.boundary: Evaluation suites are the maintainers’.

repositories.description: Jev-style calibrated decision model (Choice/Score/Noul) on Qwen3.5-0.8B
repositories.summary: Prototype of a Jev-style decision model on Qwen3.5-0.8B that forks one state encoding into many question branches.
repositories.boundary: Work in progress: temperature fitting and the stress suite had not started; architecture claims are the author’s hypotheses (README).

repositories.description: Reference implementation for Jev builders: a Claude Code hook that asks TypeSafe's Jev which skill fits each prompt and logs the answer. Run for a week, 28 of 539 suggestions used, then removed; the README keeps what transfers.
repositories.summary: Claude Code hook that asks Jev which installed skill fits each prompt and logs the answer, published with the week-long log and the analysis script.
repositories.boundary: The author removed it after a week: the log could not separate the router’s effect from the agent’s own choices.

repositories.description: Claude Code / Codex / pi plugin that hands agent steps needing no text output to Jev (TypeSafe's judgment model) — measured p50 ~230 ms and ~$0.02 per 1,000 judgments, with typed escalation back to the LLM
repositories.summary: Plugin for coding agents that hands steps needing no text output (clicks, command gating, context compaction) to Jev and escalates to the LLM when text must be written.
repositories.boundary: Latency and cost figures come from the author’s runs.

repositories.description: Calibrate Jev questions against your own labels: tune criteria on labelled examples, confirm on a held-out set, get a verdict per question. Unofficial.
repositories.summary: Tool that tunes Jev question criteria on labelled examples, confirms them on a held-out set and gives each question a verdict: act on it, sort with it, or do not use it.
repositories.boundary: The shipped example is small; verdicts are only as good as the user’s labels.

repositories.description: Open-source, local-first social media research agent for Instagram, TikTok, and LinkedIn. Jev routes read-only steps; socai CLI captures cited browser evidence.
repositories.summary: Local social-media research agent in which Jev chooses each read-only browsing step and a CLI captures cited evidence in the user’s browser.
repositories.boundary: Benchmark figures are the maintainers’.

repositories.description: Portable JevRouter setup for cost-aware Codex subagent model selection, with English and Russian instructions
repositories.summary: Codex add-on that now selects cited evidence from noisy logs deterministically; its earlier Jev-based subagent model router is kept only for reproducibility.
repositories.boundary: The author no longer recommends the Jev router after their own benchmark.

repositories.description: RLCDAlignBench: 44 alignment-failure detection benchmarks and code for 'Just Ask Jev' (RLCD zero-shot detector of AI alignment failures)
repositories.summary: RLCDAlignBench: 44 alignment-failure detection benchmarks (7,193 labelled instances across ten failure types) and the code behind the “Just Ask Jev” study.
repositories.boundary: Companion to one study (2609.29429); labels inherit from the source benchmarks.

repositories.description: GPT drives research. Jev finds evidence in parallel.
repositories.summary: Research agent in which GPT chooses what to investigate and Jev scores independent document regions in parallel to find evidence, evaluated on BrowseComp-Plus.
repositories.boundary: Small development experiments without a same-depth control that omits Jev (README).

repositories.description: Search the web with TypeSafe's Jev: source selection, query understanding and relevance ranking. Built with Search1API.
repositories.summary: Web search in which a decision model picks sources, time ranges and search terms and ranks the returned results, without generated answers.
repositories.boundary: Relevance percentages are model judgments, not verified accuracy (README).

repositories.description: Coverage, security and code quality for coding agents
repositories.summary: Coverage and code-quality tool for coding agents that scores code quality and flags security risks with Jev and turns uncovered paths into focused tasks.
repositories.boundary: Quality and risk scores are Jev judgments; coverage itself is measured without Jev.

repositories.description: Claude Code plugin that replaces the compaction summary with Jev decisions: every tool call and result is scored in one fast request, stale ones are dropped or truncated, everything kept stays verbatim.
repositories.summary: Claude Code plugin that replaces compaction summaries with Jev keep-or-drop decisions on every tool call and result, keeping what remains verbatim.
repositories.boundary: No quality evaluation reported in the README.

repositories.description: Measures how well TypeSafe's RLCD-Jev model spots real secret credentials in file snippets
repositories.summary: Scores Jev’s yes/no detection of real secret credentials in file snippets on hand-built case sets, with no regular expressions or provider checks.
repositories.boundary: Small case sets written for the test; no licence declared.

repositories.description: Semantic ifs from open models, on a 3090 at home. Independent; not affiliated with Jev or TypeSafe.
repositories.summary: Semantic ifs from frozen open models (formerly “OpenJev”): reads option-token probabilities in one pass, with prefix reuse, MLX/MPS/llama.cpp backends and per-workload temperature calibration.
repositories.boundary: Reproduces the interface pattern, not Jev’s undisclosed model or training (stated in the README). A natural training-free baseline.

repositories.summary: Small harness comparing Jev with frontier LLMs on the same structured decision tasks for accuracy, calibration, consistency, latency, cost and schema validity.
repositories.boundary: Small task set from one live run; no licence declared.

repositories.description: A nano replica of Jev: parallel decisions, dynamic candidates, and an end-to-end training pipeline.
repositories.summary: A 0.6B parallel decision model (“nano replica”) with public weights and dataset, trained on game-control decisions (ViZDoom, maze, Snake).
repositories.boundary: Game-task results do not generalise to a Jev replacement; its recorded hosted-service cohort is reused by 2609.23886.

repositories.description: Detect youtube sponsor segment with live audio and transcript powered by Jev
repositories.summary: Chrome extension that skips YouTube sponsor reads: Jev names transcript lines or answers yes/no about speech-to-text output, while code owns every timestamp.
repositories.boundary: Accuracy is measured against SponsorBlock community labels.

repositories.description: Drop-in TypeSafeClient replacement backed by LLM APIs
repositories.summary: Official drop-in replacement for the SDK’s system_one call that routes typed questions to OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini or compatible LLM APIs, for cost, speed and quality comparisons.
repositories.boundary: Answers and probabilities come from LLM structured output, not from the Jev model; useful as a matched interface baseline.

repositories.description: The official TypeScript/JavaScript library for the TypeSafe API
repositories.summary: Official TypeScript/JavaScript client for the TypeSafe API with inferred answer types.
repositories.boundary: Client only.

repositories.description: The official Python library for the TypeSafe API
repositories.summary: Official Python client for the TypeSafe API: Choice, Score and Noul questions, synchronous and asynchronous.
repositories.boundary: An open client does not make the model open; weights and training recipe are not public.

repositories.description: Add a decorator for dspy Signatures that automatically uses TypeSafe where relevant
repositories.summary: Proof-of-concept DSPy fork whose decorator sends a signature’s typed outputs through TypeSafe’s inference path without changing application code.
repositories.boundary: Proof of concept; speed and cost comparisons are the author’s.

repositories.description: Turn Any Open-LLM into a System-one Jev model
repositories.summary: Jevify: turns open LLMs into calibrated Jev-style decision models with fine-tuned readouts, released checkpoints, the jev-bench dataset and a Jev baseline with a label audit.
repositories.boundary: Leaderboard and label audit are the author’s.

repositories.summary: Personal-assistant agent with 100 mocked tools that counts the steps needed to finish a task when the LLM picks tools versus when Jev picks them.
repositories.boundary: Mocked tools; no licence declared.

repositories.summary: Starter for training small one-pass option scorers that take text and a changing list of options and return one probability per option.
repositories.boundary: A research starter, not a copy of Jev; reported accuracy comes from synthetic menus and one next-click dataset (README).

repositories.description: Laya vs Jev: local MLX and hosted AI decisions playing T-Rex side by side, with live metrics and replay recording
repositories.summary: Side-by-side T-Rex game in which local Laya on Apple Silicon and hosted Jev make each move, with live response times and crash replays.
repositories.boundary: A game demonstration; hosted Jev pays a network round trip.

repositories.description: Benchmarks and a playground for TypeSafe's Jev (System One) model: chess, and who-is-the-player-talking-to for speech-to-text game NPCs
repositories.summary: Two hands-on Jev benchmarks with every raw request and response: chess moves from 20–40 legal options, and whether a speech-to-text utterance addresses a game character.
repositories.boundary: Single author; chess lies deliberately outside the model’s strengths.

repositories.description: 5–10x faster browser operations: Jev clicks, Codex thinks and verifies. Built at EZCollegeApp.
repositories.summary: Browser skill for Codex in which Jev handles navigation, clicks, toggles and scrolling while Codex keeps text input, visual judgment and the final check.
repositories.boundary: Speed-ups are measured in the author’s own workflows.

repositories.description: Tests, calibration audits and failure-mode studies of Jev (TypeSafe System One): jaggedness, consistency, injection, abstention.
repositories.summary: Curated tests, calibration audits and failure-mode studies of Jev.
repositories.boundary: Discovery source; entries must be traced to primary evidence.

repositories.description: Turn local language models into Jev-style structured decision models. Get results from text and images with prefill alone—no token-by-token decoding required.
repositories.summary: LLM2Jev: turns local language models into Jev-style decision models from text and images with prefill alone, judging each option separately and normalising across options.
repositories.boundary: Local latency is compared with hosted Jev’s network round trip; not affiliated with TypeSafe.

repositories.description: A collection and survey of Jev
repositories.summary: Contains the public working draft “Decisions, Not Tokens”, a broader survey of machine-native decision models.
repositories.boundary: Discovery source, not evidence; link counts include unrelated infrastructure and baselines.

repositories.summary: Open-Jev: open decision models (2B–27B) that return typed probabilities for supplied candidates, with the Open-Jev training data and release reports.
repositories.boundary: In one natural-support pilot the released 2B model scored below a BM25 baseline (README).

repositories.description: Cost, accuracy and consistent correctness of Jev and nine language models on ContractNLI.
repositories.summary: Benchmark code, configurations, per-request predictions and analysis for the contract-inference study.
repositories.boundary: Not independently reproduced.

repositories.description: Turn any off-the-shelf LLM into a Jev -like decision layer
repositories.summary: LitJev: reads typed choices and probability distributions directly from the output head of off-the-shelf Qwen checkpoints, with no training and no generated text.
repositories.boundary: Inherits the base model’s accuracy and biases.

repositories.description: Local bilingual probability decisions from context, questions, and candidate answers. Independent research preview inspired by TypeSafe Jev.
repositories.summary: Open JEV: local bilingual probability decisions over candidate answers, currently read from a frozen Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 backend.
repositories.boundary: Research preview: the README claims no lead over Jev and says its probabilities are normalised label scores, not established correctness estimates.

repositories.description: Does a TypeSafe Jev rerank beat embedding search? Graded relevance eval (9,831 pairs, 164 zh/en queries) over the Agent Skills Hub catalog, with the judge-circularity bias measured.
repositories.summary: Graded relevance evaluation of Jev reranking against keyword, BM25 and embedding search over an agent-skills catalogue (9,831 labelled pairs, 164 Chinese and English queries), with judge circularity measured.
repositories.boundary: One catalogue snapshot; labels mix model judges, with each judge’s effect reported.

repositories.description: A persistent, unified memory layer for all your AI agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, DSH), backed by Markdown and Milvus.
repositories.summary: Cross-platform semantic memory layer for coding agents with optional Jev reranking of memory search results.
repositories.boundary: Jev is an optional component of a larger memory system.

repositories.description: Graph RAG with pure vector search, achieving SOTA performance in multi-hop reasoning scenarios.
repositories.summary: Graph RAG on pure vector search with an optional Jev reranker that scores and filters graph relations with shared multi-hop context.
repositories.boundary: Jev is optional; its 500-query evaluation is separate from the main results.

repositories.description: Typed-decision benchmark from PadFlow (land development SaaS): schemas, anonymized labeled rows, and a runner for confidence-calibrated models like TypeSafe Jev.
repositories.summary: Public typed-decision benchmark from a land-development software product: JSON schemas, anonymised labelled rows and a runner that scores accuracy and calibration.
repositories.boundary: Small domain set from one product.

repositories.summary: Contrastive language models (CLM): a System One model with state and action heads on a frozen Qwen3-8B encoder, trained with a bidirectional InfoNCE loss and served behind a Jev-compatible API (Choice, Noul, Score) with cached state and action embeddings.
repositories.boundary: The comparisons with Jev in the README are the maintainers’ own; an independent preregistered study found the released checkpoint near chance as a zero-shot judge (2610.07177).
repositories.notes: Training code covers fine-tuning of the heads; pre-training data are described, not released.

repositories.description: Jev-LCT: Open System-One Decision Engine with Free Calibrated Confidence from Recurrent Trajectories
repositories.summary: Jev-LCT: Qwen-based decision models that loop only the top two layers before a typed readout, read confidence from the loop trajectory, exit early on clear cases and serve a Jev-compatible API.
repositories.boundary: Benchmarks are the maintainer’s 300-item set; its own table shows the looped models at or below their single-pass backbones in accuracy (for example 81.7% against 82.7% for Qwen3-8B).
